rows.question: does the console keep a session where a script on the page can read it?

probes.expected: no session token, secret or API key written to localStorage
probes.observed: 1 storage write(s) of a credential-shaped key

unproven: the built bundle is not scanned: this reads `frontend/src`, and a vendored dependency could still write to storage at runtime
limits: The backend also sets an httpOnly `cryptoscan_session` cookie and verifies the session with GET /api/v1/auth/me, so the localStorage copy is redundant as well as exposed. Removing it means making lib/api.ts hold the token in memory and letting the cookie carry the session across a reload.

rows.question: does a credential travel in a query string?

probes.expected: no token carried in a query string

limits: The hit is `/?token=` on the invite-acceptance page: a one-time `csi_…` invitation token is read from the URL by design. It lands in browser history and in any Referer header sent from that page, and the token is single-use and server-revocable, which is why this is PARTIAL and not FAIL. A POST body would remove the exposure.
The canary proves a specific path does not echo a specific string. It cannot prove that some other path — a queue payload, a crash dump, a support bundle — does not.
Source scanning is pattern-based; a credential with no recognisable shape is invisible to it.
